A Story Kit line spoken by a person whose voice block is one of public/storykit/cast/registry.json's, with the same words as one of that voice's lines here, plays this recording (storykit/pack/registry.ts recordedClip). Credits: CREDITS.md.

lines.text: 'Delete your account.' Good morning to you too.
Okay, okay. Car, then a lawyer, then I log off forever.
Kidding. Obviously.
Yo! Banker boy! Huge fan. Sign my form?
I don't sign forms on the street. I do 'please step back'.
You've been let go. So now we're collecting something.
Hey!
Want it back? Pick up your phone. Stay humble.
Dan. Big fan. Great trades. Shame you never made any of them.
Who is this?
They call me Mr. Big. I run the bank. You ran errands.
Give it back.
Somebody has to be guilty. Your name is on every trade.
You sign the confession. Terms by text. And stop digging.
Did the CEO of my bank just ask me to confess?
Okay. You framed the wrong guy.
This is a performance review, kid! You're failing it!
Please stop hitting back! We value your feedback!
Okay! I'm escalating this to HR!
Wait! Did I miss the brief?
You always miss the brief!
Told you to check your DMs. You didn't check your DMs.
Been a little busy getting framed.
Nothing personal, kid. It's just extremely personal.
My tracker. Cut right out.
He's got my laptop. And my number.
Cool. Cool cool cool.
Don't look around. I'm not there.
You said Bryant Park.
I said bring it to Bryant Park. I'm on the library's wifi. It's free and it has a lion.
Hold the burner up. Okay. It has a twin. Same batch, same buyer.
Your face is on four front pages today. Moon's jealous.
Moon can have them. All four.
The twin pinged twenty minutes ago. A van, idling in Times Square. Seventh and Forty-Seventh.
Don't run up to it. Follow it. It'll take us to the rest of them.
Follow the van. Got it.
You're late. Sit. Burner, please.
Hi, Jane. Hi, Moon. Great to see you too.
Plugging it in. Look: two SIMs, one sale, switched on the same minute. Yours, and its twin.
My car! My beautiful leveraged car!
Keep the phone! Call it severance!
That is my door.
They know where I live.
Who's that? Liquidate him!
Wait. Banker boy? In MY yard? Liquidate him!
Everybody out of the boxes! You're all on payroll!
You can't catch Mack, banker boy!
Rook. The 'getting weird' guy.
I'm too leveraged to fight! Somebody hit him!
Shareholder value! Hit him harder!
Do you know what my bonus is riding on?
Cold-gas thrusters. Little puffs of nitrogen. Very safe. Mostly.
Define mostly.
I tested them on my van. Van's fine. It's on the roof now.
Dan. Are you watching this? JPBank's throwing a party in Washington Square.
JPBank loves New York! Free hot dogs! Free tote bags!
Right next to the Occupy camp. Now look at their screens.
It's you. Ten feet tall, three times. 'The bad apple.'
I'm going to go unplug it.
Go get your name back, kid.
Hiii, New York! JPBank loves you!
We are the ninety-nine percent!
Boo the bad apple, everybody! Booo!
Yo. That's banker boy. Protect the screens!
Wait. Why is it black? Who unplugged it?
We'll be right back! JPBank loves you! Bye!
Take your time.
Mic check!
Mic check!
Anybody the bank hates this much...
Anybody the bank hates this much!
...is somebody we should hear out!
Free Dan! Free Dan! Free Dan!
Rook. The guy who wants out.
You're back. And the car's in one piece.
Mostly.
Mostly?
Moon sleeps on Jane's feet tonight. I get a garage.
The thrusters work great. Very safe. Mostly.
Saw the park on the news. Whole camp chanting your name.
Good chanting or bad chanting?
Ha. Room's upstairs, kid. Get some sleep.
Make it look like he started it!
We saw that!
JPBank loves you! JPBank loves hot dogs! JPBank loves YOU!
Don't look at the fight! Look at the free tote bags!
This is a safe, fun, family space! Somebody hit him!
One bad apple, folks! The rest of the bank is delicious!
Banks got bailed out! We got sold out!
The whole world is watching!
We lost a screen! That's fine! We have two more! And hot dogs!
Two screens down! Still the best day ever! Somebody call legal!
Phones up, everybody! Film the men in suits!
Backup! Protect the last screen!
Hang on. Getting out.
You got out. I'll hold.
There you are. Where was I?
Welcome back. Seatbelt.
Dan. Why is your laptop doing forty down Fifth Avenue?
Because some guys in a van took it.
...Okay. I'm on the tracker. They're cutting west. Who were they?
Guys from my old job.
So, JPBank. Great, narrows it down.
Don't you have work?
I work from home. Commute's a hallway. Tracker's on my big screen.
I'll take Sixth Avenue.
Sixth goes uptown, babe. Take Ninth. It moves at six.
Love you. Getting it in before prison.
Love you too. You didn't do this. So we prove it.
Then their CEO called me. On video. From a leather chair.
Mr. Big called you? Himself?
He wants a signed confession. 'Terms by text.' Like a dentist.
You're not signing anything.
Somebody at JPBank bought Blimpco a week before the merger. With my login.
The blimp company.
Airship company. They're sensitive about it.
And the night those trades went in, you were where?
On your couch. With Moon asleep on my feet.
I know. I was right there.
So why do they want the laptop this bad?
The deal room's access log. Keeping it was my job. I kept my own copy.
Whoever logged in as me did it from the fifty-first floor.
What's on fifty-one?
Mr. Big. And his bathroom. It's a very big bathroom.
So yours is the only clean copy. Tell me you backed it up.
Bank rule. Nothing leaves the laptop.
Except the laptop.
Except the laptop.
Monday they fired me. Wednesday they charged me. Today I'm a headline.
'The face of insider trading.' At least it's a good photo.
It's my badge photo. I look like a hostage.
You looked like that at SUNY. In the library. Two a.m.
Printing my JPBank cover letter.
On my printer card. You said you'd pay me back.
Two hot dogs. I was making a statement.
The statement was mustard. It's still on my coat.
You never asked if I did it.
Since SUNY you haven't done one sneaky thing.
I took two ketchups once.
And told the cashier.
How's Moon?
Asleep on your hoodie. She ate one of your socks.
The good one?
She only eats the good ones. She misses you.
Tell her I'm on a business trip. Business is bad.
How's work?
The hospital's billing system thinks a man in Queens is a hundred and twelve and pregnant.
Is he?
He's forty and very confused. I fixed it. Nobody will ever know.
I'll know.
You're a fugitive. You don't count.
I'm not a fugitive. I'm charged. It's different.
How?
More paperwork.
What happened to the lawyer?
She read the paper and said I'm 'not a good fit'.
Lawyers say that?
They say it to guys whose face is on the paper.
Then we find one who reads logs. I'll bring the logs.
Are you driving like a banker or like a person?
What's the difference?
A banker thinks red lights are a suggestion.
I'm stopping at every light.
Liar. I can hear the rockets.
Tracker stopped. Chelsea Park, Ninth and Twenty-Eighth. Don't do anything stupid.
Define stupid.
Going there alone.
Then I'm already doing it.
Okay. The burner. Your new pen pal.
'Nice moves. Your laptop says hi. Keep this phone on.' Signed, Mr. Big.
He signs his texts. Like a birthday card.
A birthday card that wants me in prison.
Here's the thing. Burners come in batches. Same batch, same buyer.
If this one has a twin, it's in somebody's pocket. And it pings.
And you can find the ping.
I read logs for a living. I can find anything that pings.
You read hospital logs.
Hospital logs, bank logs, burner logs. Everybody leaves logs.
Also, your mom called me.
Why did my mom call you?
Because you didn't pick up. She saw the paper.
What did she say?
That you never did a bad thing in your life. Except the haircut in ninth grade.
That haircut was a choice.
She says eat something, and she believes you. In that order.
Tell her I'm eating.
Are you eating?
I'm driving past a hot dog cart. Spiritually, I'm eating.
You know what the worst part is?
The prison part?
The loans. I took this job to pay off the loans.
Seventy-eight thousand at six point eight percent.
You know my loans by heart?
I made a dashboard. It's green when you pay. It's been red since Monday.
When this is over, I'm moving in with you.
You've said that since graduation.
I was waiting for my bonus.
You were waiting for my radiator to stop clanking.
Does it still clank?
Moon sleeps against it. She thinks it's talking to her.
Where are you?
Behind a bus that says 'Smile, New York.'
Are you smiling?
I'm behind a bus. I'm doing my best.
Bryant Park, Sixth Ave side. I'm at a table. Moon's under it.
Is she guarding you?
She's guarding a pretzel.
Okay, I'm back at my table. Moon says drive safe.
Moon said that?
She sneezed. Same thing.
The twin's still on. Seventh and Forty-Seventh, idling at the curb.
Also. The Occupy camp in Washington Square made a sign about you.
Nice or mean?
It rhymes.
So, mean.
'Dan, Dan, the greedy man.'
I owe seventy-eight grand in student loans. I'm the least greedy man in Manhattan.
I know. They don't. Yet.
When you see the van, don't pull up next to it. Park, wait, let it move first.
Wait, then follow. I've seen movies.
You've seen one movie. You fell asleep.
You're taking the long way.
I'm taking the legal way.
Since when?
Since I got charged with a crime. I'm very law-abiding now.
Moon finished the pretzel.
The whole pretzel?
The whole pretzel, and a napkin. She has no regrets.
That's it. The van at the curb. Stay in the car.
Let it pull out first. Then you're a tail.
Hey. It's me. I'm whispering.
Why are you whispering?
It's a tail. You whisper on a tail.
They're in a van, Jane. A block ahead.
Then whisper louder.
I've got the van. 'JPBank Security.' On the side. Subtle.
They took my laptop, Jane. None of this is subtle.
It's registered to a Mack Moneybags. Mack. He runs Midtown for the bank's security.
Mack Moneybags. Did his parents hate him?
He picked it. He has it tattooed. In cursive.
Hang back. If they make you, they'll bolt.
They're heading west. Toward the river. Nothing out there but yards and wind.
Why would bank security need a yard?
Somewhere to put things nobody's supposed to find.
Let a car get between you. Be boring.
I'm in a car with rockets.
Be a boring car with rockets.
Mack's got a sports sedan too. Plate: MACK ONE.
Of course it is.
Leased. Everything Mack has is leased.
Even the tattoo?
Especially the tattoo.
What's Moon doing?
Watching the tracker with me. She growls when the van turns.
She's never growled in her life.
She's growling on the inside.
They're turning in. The container yard on Twelfth.
I'm hanging up before your phone rings in there.
It's on silent.
It's never on silent.
Get back in your car. The van won't wait.
Good. Find the van. Stay back.
Too close. Ease off.
You're in his mirrors. Drop back.
Dan. Back. Off.
You're losing him. Close it up a little.
Don't lose him. He's turning.
Better. Stay right there.
He made you! Go, go, don't lose him!
Going!
He's turning up Tenth. Take the corner easy.
Up Tenth! Go!
Left on Fifty-Fifth. That's the river. That's the yards.
Fifty-Fifth! Left, left!
That's Mack's car. He's heading for Herald Square.
Ram him, Dan. Gently. Ish.
There's no gentle way to ram a car.
He's got your door on his phone. Don't let that phone get away.
Not planning to.
He drives like he's late for his bonus.
He is late for his bonus. I'm making him later.
How's the car?
Fast. Loud. Possibly illegal.
Like Mack's tattoo.
Moon's barking at my screen.
Tell her I've got him.
She says you don't. She's a realist.
He just ran a red. And a yellow. And somehow a green.
How do you run a green?
Ask Mack.
I've got him on a traffic camera. He's crying.
Real tears?
Leased.
You can't catch Mack on foot! Get back in!
Go! He's getting away!
That's not gentle!
That was gentle.
Okay. That one was ish.
He's pulling away! Boost!
Don't lose him! Shift, Dan!
He's smoking! One more!
He's going down Eleventh. Past the convention center.
Left on Thirty-Fourth! He's going into traffic!
Herald Square's a mess. He's going to crash. Be there when he does.
I saw the chat. They know where you live, so you're not sleeping there tonight.
Where am I sleeping?
Gears has a room over his garage. West Chelsea. He builds rockets for cars. He's nice. Mostly.
Why not your place?
Because they've got your door. Mine's next. I'm not giving them two for one.
So where are you sleeping?
Home. With Moon and a baseball bat. Moon's the scary one.
Moon's afraid of pigeons.
The bat isn't.
Rook says he wants out.
Rook says. Let's see what Rook does.
He was the only one in that chat who said 'this is getting weird.'
He's a first-year too. Different floor, same treatment.
You know what else was in that chat? A thread called 'bonus pool.'
Security gets bonuses?
Security gets bonuses. First-years get fired three weeks before theirs.
How much was yours going to be?
Enough for a year of the loans. And a couch that isn't yours.
You love my couch.
I love your couch. Moon loves your couch. It's a crowded couch.
How was your day? Apart from me.
Apart from you, I found out why the hospital's printers print in Portuguese.
Why do they?
Someone set them to Portuguese. That was the whole mystery. It took four hours.
You love it.
I love it.
Dan. You okay?
No job, no laptop, a car with rockets. I'm great.
For real.
For real, I'm tired of being blamed. I'd like to be tired of something else.
We'll find you something else to be tired of. Promise.
That's Gears' place. Big door, loud sign. Knock twice.
Why twice?
Once, he thinks it's a delivery. Twice, he thinks it's me.
Okay. Washington Square. You know about the camp?
Occupy JPBank. Tents and drums under the arch.
Forty-one days. Bailouts, bonuses, foreclosures. They want an audit of the bank.
Every night the news shows the tents, and JPBank looks worse.
So the bank throws a party next door.
'JPBank Loves New York.' Free hot dogs, a stage, and Fiona on a megaphone.
Who's Fiona?
Head of Community. Her business card has glitter on it. Real glitter.
And three big screens on rigs on the lawn, pointed right at the tents.
Running a reel on a loop. You, ten feet tall. 'The bad apple.'
Please tell me it's not the badge photo.
It's the badge photo.
That's the pitch. The bank isn't rotten. It had one bad apple, and it caught him.
And if it's one bad apple, nobody checks the orchard.
No audit. Nobody looks at the fifty-first floor.
The reel runs off the three rigs. The big screen under the arch just mirrors them.
Kill the rigs, the reel dies.
And no reel, no bad apple.
And no bad apple, Fiona's just a lady with a megaphone and a lot of hot dogs.
Careful. The Suits are in the crowd. They'll start something and pin it on you.
So if I smash their screens at a community day, I'm the bad apple.
You're already the bad apple. Be a fast one.
One more thing. The camp's kitchen is run by Ms. Bea.
Should I know Ms. Bea?
She taught me seventh-grade science. She will not let you be rude.
I'm never rude.
Two weeks ago you walked past the camp in a suit, and a man with a drum told you to quit your job.
And then I got fired. He's a prophet. I owe him a drum.
Why is your science teacher living in a tent?
JPBank took her house. Thirty years of payments, three months late.
Three months?
Her husband was sick. The bank sent a letter. Then a locksmith.
And now a hot dog party.
And now a hot dog party.
You know the bailout paid for my training class?
Your what?
First-year training. Six weeks in a hotel ballroom. A man in a vest explaining risk.
Did he explain it?
He explained it belongs to other people.
How's Gears?
He made me breakfast and showed me a scar from a thruster.
A big scar?
He said it's a small scar on a big man.
That's the arch. Park on Fifth and walk in.
I'll be watching the broadcast. Be quick.
I'm always quick.
You're always late.
Two of their cars on you. The Village is all crooked streets. Use them.
Gears said the thrusters were very safe.
Gears says that about everything.
Break their line. Corners, Dan. Corners.
I'm cornering!
Corner harder.
Hop the traffic if you have to.
Hopping!
Did you just jump a taxi?
Very safe. Mostly.
Bea's people are filming you from the park.
Tell them to get my good side.
You're in a car.
The car is my good side.
They're gone. You lost them.
I lost them.
Don't sound so surprised.
On foot? Dan, they have cars! Get back in!
Go, go!
They've got you again. Turn!
Still on you. Next corner!
They lost you. Keep it that way.
Out of sight. Keep going.
Okay. Breathe. You're clear.
Breathing. Did it work?
The reel died mid-sentence. 'The face of insider trad—' and then black.
Good.
Better than good. The camp filmed the whole thing. Forty phones.
Bank security jumping the bank's own bad apple, at a free hot dog party.
When you put it like that, I sound innocent.
You are innocent. Now it looks like it.
Bea got on the people's mic. The whole park was chanting 'Free Dan.'
I've never had a chant.
And she crossed out 'greedy' on that sign. Now it says 'Dan, Dan, the fall man.'
That's... actually accurate.
If the camp gets its audit, the insiders go down with Mr. Big. They're panicking. At him, for once.
That's why he moved the laptop up to dawn.
And Rook's driving it. The one who wants out.
Either he wants out, or Mr. Big wants me alone in a dark park.
So we're careful.
We're never careful.
We start tonight. Go back to Gears. Eat something. Sleep an hour.
Yes, Ms. Bea.
Don't. She'd like you, by the way. She says you have a polite face.
Tell her it's the only one I've got.
Moon watched the whole thing on my laptop.
Was she proud?
She barked at Fiona and slept through the chase.
Priorities.
Your mom saw it on the news.
Which part?
The chanting. She called the station to say you're a very polite boy.
Did they put her on?
They put her on. Twice.
How many people are we talking? Chanting.
The park. And eleven thousand people watching JPBank's own broadcast.
JPBank broadcast me getting jumped by JPBank.
Live. They paid for it, too.
There's the garage. Go. Sleep.
Love you.
Love you. Go.
You're going to see Rook.
He said come alone.
He said. I didn't. I'm on the phone. That's alone-ish.
Alone-ish.
If anything feels off, you drive away. Promise me.
Promise.
What do you think Rook wants?
Out. Like he said.
Everybody wants out of something.
I don't. I like my couch.
Moon's asleep on your hoodie again.
Tell her I'm coming home soon.
She knows. She's keeping it warm.
No Rook yet.
He'll come.
Then we wait. Together. Ish.
